# Component matrix

[← Home](../README.md) · [The stack](../layers/README.md)

The 16 components builders reach for most, side by side, so an agent (or a person) can pick parts that fit together. Every cell comes from the project's own README and manifests at the commit we checked; the **Verified** column says how far we went. Nothing here was installed or run by us unless that column says so, and a green CI on this list says nothing about whether two projects work together.

**Verified:** 📄 docs at the pinned commit · 📦 installed and imported · ▶️ a documented example run.

## Cross-layer recipes

Ways to combine components across layers. The status says what kind of claim each is: 🧭 design reference (not run) · 🔗 pairing documented upstream (not run by us) · ✅ run end to end by us. A design reference is a starting point for your own integration test, not evidence that the parts work together.

### Factor research loop: RD-Agent on Qlib

**Status:** 🔗 pairing documented upstream (not run by us)

The one cross-layer pairing here that its authors document and ship: RD-Agent's quant scenarios run their factor and model proposals through Qlib's data and backtest.

1. **Harness layer** — [Qlib](https://github.com/microsoft/qlib): data store, factor evaluation and backtest
2. **Application layer** — [RD-Agent](https://github.com/microsoft/RD-Agent): proposes factors and models, writes the code, reads the results and iterates

**What you still have to build or check:** Every automatically proposed factor is another trial: count them and deflate the result (tools/evalkit), keep a held-out period the loop never sees, and add costs before believing a backtest. Upstream documents Linux and Docker for most scenarios.

**Upstream documentation:** [RD-Agent README: the Qlib scenarios](https://github.com/microsoft/RD-Agent/blob/484776c211e4fbbeef03e0ec00d6bbee7362a4f4/README.md?plain=1#L271-L286)

### Research desk whose numbers you can audit

**Status:** 🧭 design reference (not run)

Primary filings in, a written view out, and every prompt change regression-tested and traced. Two of the joins are documented upstream: FinRobot V2's SEC EDGAR provider is built on edgartools, and promptfoo can pull prompts and traces from Langfuse.

1. **Data layer** — [edgartools](https://github.com/dgunning/edgartools): pulls filings and XBRL financials as typed objects
2. **Application layer** — [FinRobot](https://github.com/AI4Finance-Foundation/FinRobot): computes the figures with code and lets the model write around them
3. **Harness layer** — [promptfoo](https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo): regression tests for the research prompts, including prompt injection through filing text
4. **Harness layer** — [Langfuse](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse): traces every run with its inputs, tool calls and cost

**What you still have to build or check:** Not run end to end by us. Feeding FinRobot's runs into promptfoo tests and Langfuse traces is your work: neither project documents it. Record each filing's acceptance time, not the fetch time, and check the generated text against the computed numbers.

**Upstream documentation:** [FinRobot V2 depends on edgartools](https://github.com/AI4Finance-Foundation/FinRobot/blob/63e1884a42ea7b729551a5424b4bd6a65af636e0/finrobot_desktop/pyproject.toml?plain=1#L40) · [promptfoo's Langfuse integration](https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/blob/e48ed85e08ff8a1ca74fa7d0e41daf47cf155efb/site/docs/integrations/langfuse.md?plain=1#L6-L38)

### Paper-trading agent with guardrails

**Status:** 🧭 design reference (not run)

A decision framework that stops at a rating, an order tool that defaults to paper, and the ledger in between that neither ships.

1. **Data layer** — [OpenBB](https://github.com/OpenBB-finance/OpenBB): market and fundamental data for the analysts
2. **Agent layer** — [TradingAgents](https://github.com/TauricResearch/TradingAgents): analyst debate that ends in a five-tier rating
3. **Execution layer** — [Alpaca MCP Server](https://github.com/alpacahq/alpaca-mcp-server): paper orders, with ALPACA_TOOLSETS restricted to the tools the agent needs
4. **Harness layer** — [Langfuse](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse): a trace of each decision, tool call and order

**What you still have to build or check:** Not run end to end by us. TradingAgents emits ratings, not orders: position sizing, order-value and exposure limits in code, and reconciliation of intended against filled orders are yours to build. Paper fills are kinder than live ones, and one environment flag switches Alpaca to real money.
